Skittish and shy, the frondilli is a fleeting sight in the colder timberlands of Last Bloom. With utmost caution, as its frail and small 
form is easy prey for many predators within the Wealdwoods, the small deer quietly approaches deciduous trees with practiced haste, 
scratching and digging into the bark with its wedge-like razored jaw. With deep rents cutting into the bark, it will lick its fi ll of the thick 
calorie-rich flowing sap. Easily camouflaged in the dense underbrush with its leaf-like green tinged fur, cautiously listening for the 
slightest potential danger, its sensitive ears swiveling back and forth to hear in all directions. At the slightest snap of a twig or muffled 
crunch of snow, it will flee deeper into the woods, hidden away beneath concealing brush and branch. 
Class - Mammalia • Genus Derived Evolution - Cervus • Niche - Specialist Gummivore

Encountering Wary of any and all other creatures, the frondilli 
will either flee long before being seen or hide in the underbrush 
using its natural camouflage. Outside of the mating months an 
adult deer will often be found grazing alone or in pairs if they 
are caring for young fawn. It is possible for a Traveler to lure a 
frondilli with the rich aroma of syrups or sap, but it will quickly 
escape from the slightest sign of danger.
